corrected_value.title: Common genetic variation near melatonin receptor MTNR1B contributes to raised plasma glucose and increased risk of type 2 diabetes among Indian Asians and European Caucasians

decisions.location: Methods, Statistical analyses (lines 9-10); Results (lines 16-17); References ref. 5 (line 102); ESM Table 2 (line 133)
decisions.quote:
The MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs (ESM Table 2) for a total of 29 SNPs that we attempted to replicate in our African-American cohort.
Our replication effort occurred in two stages. In the first stage, we attempted to replicate 20 of the 29 exact published SNPs (i.e. direct replication) available in the HUFS dataset. For this stage, SNPs were considered replicated if the same HUFS SNP had a p value <0.05. For the second stage, we performed a local replication analysis based on a 500 kb linkage disequilibrium (LD) block containing a query SNP determined by the SNPs most distant from the query SNP with r 2 ≥0.3. We used the HapMap CEU LD data (http://hapmap.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ downloads/ld_data/2008-06/00README.TXT) for all SNPs except for rs2166706 where the Gujarati Indians in Houston, Texas, USA (GIH) reference dataset (http:// hapmap.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/downloads/ld_data/2008-09_ phaseIII/00README.txt) was used to match the original reported GWAS population [5].
decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests the fasting plasma glucose (FPG) association of SNP rs2166706 near MTNR1B (11q21) reported by Chambers et al. (2009) (ref. [5], Diabetes 58:2703-2708; ESM Table 2 line 133, Excel serial date 40028.0 = 2009-08-04) in 927 unrelated non-diabetic African-American participants from the Howard University Family Study (HUFS). Specifically, rs2166706 was one of the 13 additional SNPs from prior GWASs included in the 29-SNP replication pool, was directly tested in Stage 1 (failing to reach p < 0.05, as Results line 16 reports that SNPs from remaining studies that did not directly replicate are not shown), and was specifically queried in Stage 2 local LD-based replication using the HapMap GIH reference panel to match the original Indian Asian discovery population of ref. [5]. This original study is distinct from the sole shipped row (873, Dupuis et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42:105-116, doi:10.1038/ng.520, which tested MAGIC meta-analysis SNP rs10830963 at MTNR1B) and from sibling target 2 (Bouatia-Naji et al. 2008, Nat Genet, which reported rs1387153 at MTNR1B in European cohorts) as well as targets 3-6. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests the fasting plasma glucose (FPG) association of SNP rs1387153 near MTNR1B (11q21) reported by Bouatia-Naji et al. (ESM Table 2 line 134, PubMed ID 19060909, Nat Genet, Excel serial date 39789.0 = 2008-12-07, giving year 2008) in 927 African-American participants from the HUFS cohort. In Methods (lines 9-10), the authors state that the 16 MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs listed in ESM Table 2 for a total of 29 SNPs attempted for replication via Stage 1 direct replication (rs1387153 had no 'c' exclusion footnote and did not achieve p < 0.05; Results line 16) and Stage 2 500 kb LD-block local replication. This work is an independent GWAS discovery paper distinct from the sole shipped row (873, Dupuis et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42:105-116, doi:10.1038/ng.520, the later MAGIC meta-analysis testing rs10830963 at MTNR1B) and from sibling target 1 (Chambers et al. 2009, Diabetes, testing rs2166706 in Indian Asians and Europeans) as well as targets 3-6. Author and year fields reflect the exact metadata printed in ESM Table 2. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests two fasting plasma glucose (FPG) SNP associations reported by Meigs et al. (ESM Table 2 lines 136-137, PubMed ID 17903298, BMC Med Genet, Excel serial date 39344.0 = 2007-09-19, giving year 2007): rs2722425 in ZMAT4 (8p11.21) and rs180730 in PRDM5 (4q27). In the HUFS African-American cohort, rs2722425 was directly replicated in Stage 1 (β = 0.01326, p = 0.024; Results line 16, Table 1 line 47) and locally replicated via three LD proxies in Stage 2 (including rs1823643, corrected p = 0.007; Table 2 lines 93-95), whereas rs180730 did not replicate (Results line 16). Discussion (line 21) explicitly contrasts ZMAT4 with the shipped MAGIC meta-analysis (row 873, Dupuis et al. 2010), noting that ZMAT4 was 'identified in previous GWASs but not replicated in the MAGIC meta-analysis'. Meigs et al. (2007) in BMC Med Genet is also a distinct paper reporting different SNPs and analyses from sibling target 5 (Florez et al. 2007, Diabetes, PubMed ID 17848626, which integrated multi-cohort replication datasets and reported 7 completely different SNPs including rs625643) as well as targets 1-3 and 6. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests the association at the IRS1 locus (rs2943641, 2q36.3) reported by Rung et al. (ESM Table 2 line 145, PubMed ID 19734900, Nat Genet, Excel serial date 40062.0 = 2009-09-06, giving year 2009) in the HUFS African-American cohort. Although the exact index SNP rs2943641 was unavailable for Stage 1 direct comparison due to quality-control/imputation filters (Results line 16, ESM Table 2 footnote c), it was empirically re-tested in Stage 2 local LD-based replication querying SNPs with r^2 >= 0.3 in a 500 kb window around rs2943641, yielding 10 statistically significant LD proxy SNPs near IRS1 after Bonferroni correction (Table 2 lines 83-92, including rs2972149 with corrected p = 0.004; Results line 17; Discussion line 21: 'Using the local (LD-based) replication strategy, we replicated additional SNPs in or near previously reported genes, including the insulin receptor substrate 1 gene'). Rung et al. (2009) is an independent original GWAS distinct from the sole shipped row (873, Dupuis et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42:105-116, doi:10.1038/ng.520, which did not include IRS1 among its 16 FPG loci) and from sibling targets 1-5. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.
